chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a man were brought to me who had slandered a Muslim servant with adultery, and we know nothing of him except goodness, I would strike him with the penalty, the penalty of a free man, except for one lash.'

key_terms.حَدَّ الْحُرِّ: The penalty of a free man

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for slandering a Muslim servant?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the hadd penalty for qadhf against a Muslim servant is reduced by one lash compared to a free man, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse 24:4 which specifies 'ninety lashes' for the servant. This narration, found in al-Kafi, highlights the juristic principle that the status of the accused affects the severity of the punishment, even when the slanderer is a person of known integrity ('known for his goodness').

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘If they come up to measws with a man who slandered a Muslim servant with the adultery, not being known from him except for the goodness, Iasws would strike him with the Penalty (Hadd), a Penalty (Hadd) of the free (man) except for one lash (less)’.
